question.text: Income from commodity derivative trading that is classified as speculative income is treated as:

answer.text: Speculative business income — with restrictions on set-off against non-speculative income
Capital gains — taxed at special rates

explanation.text: The Logic: When commodity derivative trading is classified as speculative under the Income-tax Act, the resulting gain or loss is treated as speculative business income. The key consequence is that speculative losses can only be set off against speculative profits and are not freely available to offset normal business or other heads of income. The Trap: Speculative derivative trading is not taxed as capital gains, is not exempt as agricultural income, and is not tax-free — it is a separately ring-fenced category of business income. Note: The Series XVI Commodity Derivatives workbook pages reviewed explain speculative futures positions but do not state the speculative-business-income classification or the loss-set-off restriction. The framing above reflects general Indian income-tax practice rather than a workbook citation.
